procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and order of the High Court of Orissa at Cuttack dated 10.12.2020, dismissing Writ Appeal No. 435/2020 and affirming the order of the learned Single Judge dated 14.01.2020.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellants preferred a writ appeal before the Division Bench of the High Court against the order of the learned Single Judge. The Division Bench found no merit in the appeal and dismissed it, affirming the Single Judge's order.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellants approached the Supreme Court questioning the judgment and order of the High Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order, dismissed the writ petition filed by the respondent, and affirmed the punishment of compulsory retirement awarded to the respondent.

decision.sentence_status: The punishment of compulsory retirement awarded to the respondent is affirmed.

cases.principle: The enumeration of particular matters in a sub-section specifying rule-making powers does not control or limit the width of the general rule-making powers conferred by the main sub-section of that provision.

cases.case_name: State of Jammu and Kashmir v. Lakhwinder Kumar and Ors.
cases.principle: For a rule framed under a statute to have statutory force, it must (1) conform to the provisions of the statute under which it is framed, and (2) come within the scope of the rule-making power of the authority. If either condition is not met, the rule is void.

cases.case_name: Rohtak & Hissar Districts Electric Supply Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.principle: It was relied upon for the principle that rules framed under a statute must conform to the provisions of that statute and be within the scope of the rule-making power to be valid and have statutory force.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: Rules framed under the provisions of a statute have statutory force only if two conditions are fulfilled: (1) the rule must conform to the provisions of the statute under which it is framed; and (2) the rule must come within the scope and purview of the rule-making power of the authority framing it. A rule that fails to meet either of these conditions is void.
obiter: The intention of the legislature, as indicated in the enabling Act, must be the prime guide to the extent of a delegate’s power to make rules; the delegate must not travel wider than the object of the legislature.
A delegate cannot override an Act by exceeding the authority or by making provisions inconsistent with the Act, unless the enabling Act itself permits its modification by the rules.
